content: Take four tablets orally every six hours with liquid. Administer two tablespoons orally every 12 hours for three to four days, then reduce to one to two tablespoons at bedtime. Ensure that eight ounces of fluid are consumed with each dose. This regimen is intended for constipation but is not recommended for use in children. For children, administer one to two tablespoons in milk or cereal orally once daily or every 12 hours for three to four days, then reduce to one to two tablespoons at bedtime. Again, ensure eight ounces of fluid are taken with each dose. For single feedings, administer one to two teaspoons. Malt soup extract and deflazacort both reduce serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor potassium levels closely. Malt soup extract decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown, but close monitoring is advised. Potential adverse effects include flatulence, fecal impaction, excessive bowel activity, hypersensitivity reactions, nausea, vomiting, bowel obstruction, appendicitis, dysphagia, fecal impaction, and rectal bleeding. Before administration, gastrointestinal obstruction or perforation must be ruled out. Exercise caution in patients with severe active ulcerative colitis. Regarding pregnancy, this medication is classified as Category B, meaning that controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. For lactation, there is no available data, but as the medication is not absorbed systemically, it is unlikely to pose a risk to breastfeeding infants.
